build an rpg and farming simulator: Farming & Animal Husbandry

​Crops: Planting, watering, and harvesting seasonal crops (e.g., strawberries in Spring, blueberries in Summer, pumpkins in Fall).

​Livestock: Raising chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs. Animals produce goods that can be converted into artisan products (like turning milk into cheese or truffles into truffle oil).

​Farm Types: At the start, you choose a farm layout tailored to different playstyles-from classic agricultural plots to riverland fishing spots or wilderness maps with monsters.

​⛏️ Mining & Combat

​The Mines: A 120-floor subterranean system filled with ores (copper, iron, gold, iridium), gemstones, and hostile monsters.

​Combat: Simple real-time sword and weapon combat used to clear floors, gather crafting materials, and discover deeper underground locations like the Skull Cavern.

​🎣 Fishing & Foraging

​Fishing: A skill-based minigame that changes depending on the weather, season, time of day, and water body (ocean, river, mountain lake).

​Foraging: Gathering wild berries, mushrooms, and trees across the map to craft supplies and fences.

​💬 Social Life & Town Dynamics

​Pelican Town: Home to over 30 unique villagers, each with their own schedules, cutscenes, backstories, and personalities.

​Relationships: You can talk to villagers, give them gifts, participate in seasonal town festivals, and even marry one of the 12 eligible bachelors or bachelorettes.

​Roommates & Family: You can build a home, have children with a spouse, or ask Krobus (a friendly shadow monster) to move in as a roommate.

answers.ask: No look was stated - should the valley read as soft storybook countryside, or grounded rustic realism?
answers.answer: Use a soft storybook countryside look, matching the cozy farming RPG tone.

answers.ask: Is the mine a real 120 floors, or a handful of floors that repeat with depth? 120 built floors is a different build entirely.
answers.answer: Make it a real 120-floor mine, as specified, with floors progressing through the stated ore tiers and deeper areas.

answers.ask: Does each player get their own farm, or does one server share a single farm?
answers.answer: Each player gets their own farm so they can choose and develop their selected farm layout independently.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No look was stated - should the valley read as soft storybook countryside, or grounded rustic realism? A: Use a soft storybook countryside look, matching the cozy farming RPG tone.
- [author] scale — Q: Is the mine a real 120 floors, or a handful of floors that repeat with depth? 120 built floors is a different build entirely. A: Make it a real 120-floor mine, as specified, with floors progressing through the stated ore tiers and deeper areas.
- [author] shape — Q: Does each player get their own farm, or does one server share a single farm? A: Each player gets their own farm so they can choose and develop their selected farm layout independently.
- [agent_inferred] mine decomposition — Q: How can 120 real floors be captured authoritatively? A: Build 120 compact sequential mine-floor maps linked downward, rather than one visually occluded 120-level stack.
- [agent_inferred] ore progression — Q: How do the four stated ore tiers occupy 120 floors? A: Use four 30-floor bands: copper, iron, gold, then iridium and the deepest cavern.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a soft storybook farming-RPG world with a shared countryside town and independent player farm maps. Provide three selectable farm templates: classic crop plots, riverland ground with fishing channels, and wilderness farmland with monster encounter clearings. Every farm supports seasonal strawberry, blueberry, and pumpkin fields; pens for chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs; artisan-processing space; and a farmhouse footprint. In the shared valley, arrange a cozy town for over 30 villagers, connected foraging ground, and ocean, river, and mountain-lake fishing spots. Connect the valley to a real 120-floor mine built as compact sequential floor maps, with visible ore and gemstone ground progressing through 30-floor copper, iron, gold, and iridium/deep-cavern bands.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation for farming and animal husbandry, with RPG secondary for town life, progression, mining, and combat.

## Shape and preset
Use a described shape: a shared valley and town linked to isolated per-player farm maps and 120 sequential mine maps. `plot-isolated` misses the shared town and mine; `world-hub-dungeon` misses the independent farm templates. Set `enclosure` to transition, `zone-count` to multi-zone, and leave `verticality` single-surface per decomposed map, `structure` dressed, and `play-space` grounded-surface. Preset: none.

## Config requirements
Use `trigger-task` visibly as crop plots, five livestock pens per farm, and artisan work areas. Use `safezone-town` and `settlement-density` for the shared storybook town. Use `path-circulation` for valley and farm routes. Use `hazard-aggro` for wilderness and mine encounter ground. Use `water-body` for ocean, river, and mountain lake. Use `terrain-relief` for the valley and mountain-lake slopes. Use the visible half of `npc-population` for over 30 villagers. Use the visible half of 120 `teleporter-link` pairs as a valley mine entrance followed by compact downward mine lifts between sequential floor maps.

## Layout requirements
Place `trigger-task` farming and husbandry interactions in every instantiated farm. Place `npc-population` as over 30 scheduled villager positions throughout town. Place `collectible-nodes` across foraging ground and on every mine floor, matched to the four 30-floor ore bands. Place `spawner-npc` in wilderness-farm clearings and across hostile mine floors. Place 120 `teleporter-link` pairs: one from the valley entrance to Mine Floor 1 and 119 linking each floor to its successor through Mine Floor 120.

## Layout components
The Shared Valley map segment uses `world-open` for the town, foraging ground, and three fishing-water types. The farm-map family uses `plot-isolated` across three templates—Classic Farm, Riverland Farm, and Wilderness Farm—instantiated independently per player; each contains crop fields, five livestock types, artisan areas, and a farmhouse footprint. Mine Floor 1 through Mine Floor 120 are 120 separate compact `space-bounded` map segments advancing through four 30-floor material bands. The shared town contains over 30 villagers.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: the shared valley, farm templates, water access, and 120-floor sequence must be authoritative before storybook dressing.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by independent farms, a shared valley, and 120 real mine floors. The theme is soft storybook countryside with progressively deeper mines. Use `P4` for separate farms and mine floors, `P3` for outdoor-to-mine transitions, `CHECK` for fishing water, and `tiered` for valley relief.
